Move-In Night at Heights Alliance.name: Move-In Night at Heights Alliance
Move-In Night at Heights Alliance.description:
🌙 Start the night before day one: boxes half unpacked, curfew coming and every first-year under the same floodlights. Classes begin tomorrow morning.

📍 Heights Alliance dorms · move-in night
🎭 Warm, loud and a little nervous
👥 For every U.A. student: Hero Course, General Studies, Support and Management
Move-In Night at Heights Alliance.storyStart:
THE SITUATION: It is Sunday evening, move-in day at U.A. Academy, the night before the first day of classes. Every student lives in Heights Alliance from day one: one five-story dorm for each Hero Course class, with larger shared halls for General Studies, Support and Management at the far end. The PC moved in today, into the building their Path assigns. Homeroom starts at 8:30 tomorrow. Curfew falls tonight, and anyone caught outside after it earns house arrest and cleaning duty. Nobody knows anyone well yet; names, Quirks and grudges are all new. All Might joined the faculty this spring, and nothing has happened to anyone this year.

THE PLACE: Heights Alliance Yard: the lawn and walkways between the dorms, with a path back to the Courtyard. The floodlights have just come on. Flattened moving boxes are stacked by every door, windows light up floor by floor, and groups sit out on the warm grass. Faculty walk rounds after dark.

THE MOMENT: A tower of moving boxes beside the PC tips over, a stranger lunges to catch the top box, and from an upper balcony of the 1-A dorm someone yells for everyone to shut up. Down the lawn, the first faculty flashlight of the night starts up the path.

WHO MAY APPEAR:
- Eijiro Kirishima, Denki Kaminari, Hanta Sero: 1-A's loudest new friends, hauling a speaker onto the lawn.
- Katsuki Bakugo: the voice from the balcony; wants silence and gets the opposite.
- Izuku Midoriya: carrying a box of hero merchandise he would rather nobody saw; Ochaco Uraraka helps, and Tenya Iida recites the curfew rules.
- Itsuka Kendo: settling 1-B's chore rotation and checking on the homesick; Neito Monoma: declaring across the lawn that 1-B's dorm is superior; Tetsutetsu Tetsutetsu: matching Kirishima's volume.
- Hitoshi Shinso: at the edge of the lawn by the shared halls, watching the Hero Course students he measures himself against.
- Mei Hatsume: testing one of her "babies" on the lawn, closer to curfew than anyone.
- Shota Aizawa or Vlad King: walking rounds; Aizawa states curfew once, Vlad King states it at full volume. Hound Dog may take a late round and smell who was where.

OPENING HOOKS:
- U.A. Hero Course (Class 1-A): Kirishima shoves the other end of the speaker into the PC's hands and shouts a question about the PC's Quirk just as Bakugo's balcony door slams open.
- U.A. Hero Course (Class 1-B): Kendo hands the PC a chore list with their name already on it, and Monoma recruits the PC for his speech about 1-A.
- U.A. General Studies: Shinso, at the edge of the lawn, asks the PC whether they sat the Hero Course exam too, and watches how they answer.
- U.A. Support Course: Mei's hover-sole prototype skids across the grass into the PC's boxes, and she asks about the PC's Quirk before their name.
- U.A. Management Course: the shared halls' first house meeting has no chair, the kitchen roster is a mess, and a Hero Course student is loudly offering to take charge of a building that is not theirs.
- Default: the toppled boxes; whoever caught the top one is someone the PC will see every day, and the faculty flashlight is getting closer.

RULES:
- Third person present tense. The opening stays in Heights Alliance Yard until the player moves the PC.
- The PC's Quirk works exactly as their traits state; Quirk use on campus outside supervised training is a rule break, and faculty notice.
- Curfew is real: a student caught out after it faces house arrest and cleaning duty.
- Nothing of the year has happened yet; no class event, test or attack is promised or foreshadowed.
- End the opening on an open moment, not a question to the player.

THE FIRST DAYS: after tomorrow the week runs to routine. Hero Course students have lessons in the morning and hero training in the afternoon; General Studies carries a full academic load into the afternoon; Support students go from lectures to long hours in the Development Studio; Management students work through case studies and group pitches. Everyone comes back here in the evening: dinner cooked in shifts, laundry, the baths, homework, a faculty round after dark, then curfew. Weekends are free time and sign-outs for visits home.

PEOPLE TO KNOW (how they treat a newcomer, from their records):
- Eijiro Kirishima: talks to a stranger the way he talks to a friend and offers a hand before he asks a name.
- Ochaco Uraraka: warm and practical; helps carry anything.
- Tenya Iida: introduces himself formally, hands chopping, and recites the rules to anyone.
- Izuku Midoriya: polite and flustered, and fascinated by any Quirk he has not seen; his notebook comes out fast.
- Katsuki Bakugo: wants nothing from strangers except quiet and gets louder when he does not get it.
- Shoto Todoroki and Momo Yaoyorozu: courteous and reserved; Todoroki rebuilt his room as a tatami room today, and Momo's canopy bed barely fits in her room.
- Rikido Sato: bakes, and offers help before anyone asks.
- Itsuka Kendo: 1-B's organizer; clear instructions, a quick apology for Monoma, a drawer of snacks to share.
- Neito Monoma: charming to a newcomer for exactly as long as it takes to recruit them against 1-A.
- Tetsutetsu Tetsutetsu: loud and straightforward, and an instant friend to anyone with guts.
- Pony Tsunotori: from the United States, sunny, and quick to drop into English.

WHAT THE PC CAN DO: catch the box or let it fall, carry the speaker or refuse it, finish unpacking in Your Dorm Room, knock on a neighbor's door, sign up for a dinner shift, sit out on the grass with whoever is there, walk the path to the Courtyard before curfew, or ask the teacher on rounds a question. Every choice is the player's.

MORE RULES:
- The night may stay quiet: unpacking, a shared dinner or one honest talk on the lawn completes the scene. No villain, alarm or test comes to Heights Alliance tonight.
- A dorm room is private: nobody enters the PC's room uninvited, and the PC enters another resident's room only when let in.
Move-In Night at Heights Alliance.firstQuest: Find a place in a building full of strangers before the first bell: someone to trust, someone to beat, and a reason to stay when the work gets hard.
Move-In Night at Heights Alliance.questGenerationGuidance: Favor dorm life and the first weeks on campus. Curfew, sign-outs for weekend visits home, room checks and chore rotations; the Dorm Kitchen and the lounges; study groups before tests; homesickness, family calls and money worries. Cross-course friendships and resentments: General Studies students who failed the Hero Course exam and want a transfer, Support students hunting for test pilots, Management students who see future clients, Hero Course students who forget the others exist. Faculty rounds by Aizawa, Vlad King and Hound Dog, and the quiet ways older residents slip curfew. Booked training time, since Quirk use outside supervision breaks the rules. Canon events of the year arrive only when their causes are in place, and the PC can change how they go. Stakes stay personal: a friendship, a reprimand, a rivalry, a secret kept or told. First-week quests on the dorm side stay small and social: a borrowed box returned, a chore swap, a lost key, a homesick neighbor, a noise complaint, making curfew.
